artworks.title: Black-billed Cuckoo
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of birds interacting with magnolia flowers. Two brown birds are featured amidst lush green foliage and large white magnolia flowers, with one bird perched upside down on a branch and the other extending its wing. There are also brown and green leaves displaying details like veins and small holes. A small insect hovers near the flowers. The flowers themselves are depicted in stages from bud to bloom, showcasing their creamy petals and texture. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Yellow Bird or American Goldfinch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds among thistle plants. One bird has vibrant yellow and black colors, while the other has brown and yellow tones. The color palette includes bright yellows, deep greens, muted browns, and hints of pink and purple from the thistle flowers. The birds are positioned in the top left and below, interacting with the thistle plants that stretch diagonally across the image.

artworks.title: Worm-eating Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched among branches with green leaves and clusters of berries. One bird has its beak open, while the other is inspecting the berries. The branches have green leaves with a few dried ones. The berries are dark, some turning red. The birds and leaves are intricately detailed, resembling the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Children's Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a branch with yellow flowers. The artwork shows two small birds on a leafy branch with clusters of yellow blossoms. Each bird is depicted in a naturalistic posture, engaging with its surroundings. The branch is adorned with green leaves and buds, creating a sense of growth. The background is plain, highlighting the intricate detailing of the birds and flora. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Stanley Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds: two hawks and a smaller blue bird. One hawk is perched on a piece of wood while the other is in flight. The hawk in flight has brown feathers with white markings, while the perched hawk has grey and tan colors. The smaller blue bird has vibrant blue feathers and a reddish-brown chest, appearing to be in mid-flight. The focus is on naturalistic details, particularly on feather patterns and textures, in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Gold-winged Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of four woodpeckers interacting on a tree branch. The image features detailed renderings of woodpeckers in various poses and activities. One woodpecker is perched on a vertical broken tree trunk with an open beak, while another hangs upside down on a branch, displaying bright yellow underwings. Another woodpecker is seen peeking around the tree trunk with a caterpillar in its beak, and the fourth woodpecker is sitting calmly on a horizontal branch. The feathers and tree bark are depicted with detailed textures and vivid coloration. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon, known for his studies and artistic representations of birds.

artworks.title: Kentucky Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds with bright yellow undersides and green and black tops perched on a plant branch with large green leaves and tan flowers. The colors in the image are various shades of green, yellow, and tan against a neutral background. A small spider is visible towards the bottom left hanging from a thin strand.

artworks.title: Crested Titmouse
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting shows two birds perched on a pine branch. The birds have distinct coloring and postures, with one facing downward and the other shown from below. The branch is detailed with cones and needles, and the background is blank. The text identifies the birds as "Crested Titmouse," with a scientific notation of "Parus Bicolor." The artwork is created in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: American Redstart
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of American Redstarts and a wasp nest. The image shows two birds perched on branches surrounded by green leaves, with a wasp nest hanging below them. One bird is in mid-flight with black, orange, and white plumage, while the other bird is perched on a branch showing yellow markings on its back. The wasp nest is detailed with hexagonal patterns, and several wasps are crawling on it.

artworks.title: Ruffed Grouse
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This image shows three birds in a natural setting. The painting depicts detailed foliage and scattered leaves, with two birds in the foreground showcasing plumage of reddish-brown, grey, blue, and green. One bird appears to be reaching towards a bunch of dark berries on a thin branch. The background features green leaves and moss-covered branches. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for realistic portrayals of birds.

artworks.title: Orchard Oriole
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows several colorful birds around a nest on a tree branch. The birds have bright colors like black, red, yellow, and orange, against a pale background highlighting the green leaves. The nest is woven into the branch, with birds positioned around it.

artworks.title: Cedar Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a juniper branch. The birds are brown and gray with yellow and red accents on their wings and tails, as well as a black face mask. The branch has green needle-like foliage and round berries. The background is soft and neutral, emphasizing the colors and details of the birds and foliage.

artworks.title: Summer Red Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three birds perched on a branch with large leaves and dark berries. The largest bird at the top is bright red with black markings around its wings and tail. Below it is a smaller bird with a yellow body and some dark feathers on its wings. The third bird near the bottom also has red plumage with green highlights on its wings. The color palette includes red, yellow, green, and dark purple. The red bird is at the top, the yellow bird is in the middle, and the third bird is at the bottom left.

artworks.title: Traill's Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a leafy branch. The painting depicts a small bird with its beak open on a stalk entwined with green leaves. The bird's feathers and the details of the leaves are intricately portrayed. The background is a plain, pale surface.

artworks.title: Ruby-throated Humming Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: Cerulean Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds on a branch with red berries and leaves. The birds are primarily blue with white and black accents, perched on a branch against a cream-colored background.

artworks.title: Blue-green Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a blue-green bird perched on a branch of a plant with clusters of pink berries. The image features a bird sitting upon a branch with leaves and pink berries. The bird has blue plumage with black-and-white markings. The plant is labeled as "Spanish Mulberry." The background is simple to emphasize the details of the bird and plant. The illustration showcases precision in depicting the bird and foliage in a botanical style.

artworks.title: Swainson's Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Swainson's Warbler perched on a branch with large green leaves and acorns. The painting depicts a small bird with a blend of gray, yellow, and black plumage, showcasing the intricate details of its feathers, particularly the white and black pattern along its wings. The branch it is perched on extends diagonally across the canvas, with large, textured leaves of a vibrant green hue. Nestled among the leaves are a few clustered acorns. The overall composition highlights the bird’s stance and the botanical features with attention to detail.

artworks.title: Red Tailed Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two hawks in combat over a hare. The upper hawk has vibrant red tail feathers and intricate patterns of brown, black, and white on its wings, displaying a sense of intense motion and aggression. The lower hawk lies across, its body and wings horizontal, adding tension and drama to the composition. The hare appears lifeless, with a notable detail of red staining near its midsection, indicating a struggle. In the background, a faint outline of distant mountains can be seen. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Chuck Will's Widow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds and a snake interacting on a branch. The birds have elaborately patterned feathers and are perched on a branch alongside a vibrantly colored snake. The snake has black, red, and yellow bands and appears to be slithering along the branch. There are green leaves and bright pink buds surrounding the birds and snake. The painting combines a naturalistic portrayal of the wildlife subjects with a focus on detailed textures and colors.

artworks.title: Painted Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts colorful birds, called "Fringilla Ciris" or Painted Buntings, on a branch. The birds have vibrant plumage in shades of blue, red, and green, set against a plain background. They are shown in various poses on a leafy branch with green berries, including one bird holding a thread in its beak. The style of the painting is reminiscent of the detailed realism of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Rice Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on branches with hanging red seeds. The painting features a black and white bird with intricate brown patterning on its wings and a pale orange patch around its neck standing atop a branch adorned with vibrant red, maple-like samaras. Below, another smaller bird with an olive and beige plumage appears poised as if about to leap from another branch. The branches are sparsely filled with clusters of winged seeds cascading downward, offering a splash of vivid color against the subdued backdrop.

artworks.title: Cuvier's Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A small bird with a red crown and intricate markings on its wings is perched on the branch of a flowering plant. The plant features large green leaves and clusters of pink flowers with star-shaped patterns. The background is a pale, light cream color. The bird is perched on a horizontal branch, surrounded by leaves and flowers both above and below it. The illustration's title and scientific labels are located in the lower right corner.

artworks.title: Red-shouldered Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two red-shouldered hawks perched on a branch. The hawks are detailed, showing patterns on their feathers in shades of brown, red, and grey. They have sharp beaks and intense eyes. The background is plain, emphasizing the birds' colorful feathers. Branches with leaves and a vine are depicted. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's bird illustrations.
